advisory.finding: New test `test_fit_comment_is_the_text_the_send_path_lands` parametrizes over rich=[False,True] and builds its `expected` from `AdfCodec(rich=rich)`, but `_JiraSanitizer.fit_comment` internally uses `AdfCodec(rich='cloud' in cutover_clients())` which is governed by ambient config (ships 'off' => rich=False), and this test applies NO cutover-pinning fixture. The rich=True case therefore compares a config-governed (default rich=False) fit against a hardcoded rich=True expectation.
merged_from: test_fit_comment_is_the_text_the_send_path_lands parametrizes rich=[False, True] and derives its expected value from an explicit AdfCodec(rich=rich), but _JiraSanitizer.fit_comment resolves its codec mode internally from cutover_clients() (ambient config, no fixture pins it in this test; default ships 'off' -> rich=False). The rich=True case therefore never exercises fit_comment's rich-mode fit branch: it will either fail (if the two modes cut the body differently) or pass only because both modes coincide for these bodies, so the parametrization gives false confidence and the rich-mode convergence contract is untested against fit_comment.
scenarios: Running the suite with the shipped default rich_text_cutover=off while the rich=True fixture bodies serialize differently under fit_markdown_to_adf_limit vs fit_text_to_adf_limit
CI environment where marklas is installed so rich/plain fits diverge
